name: Configuration Management Console
description: Freezes the UX for the configuration console FF-EPIC-17/18 has no UI for: a settings editor that states where every value came from, a key catalog that states what every key is, and the secret + audit surfaces that make changes safe and attributable. Approving these frames approves the visual model AND the build inventory (flows / components / packages), so implementation cannot quietly invent a different architecture. The load-bearing states are contract, not decoration: locked-by-ancestor naming the ancestor from lockedBy, system-hidden keys ABSENT rather than filtered, unset vs pin-the-parent's-value as two distinct operations, VERSION_CONFLICT driving re-read-and-merge instead of blind retry, stale-value-vs-updated-definition, and secret reveal-once.

frames.label: (a) Settings editor
frames.summary: The populated editor: scope chain switcher, namespace, categorised rows with typed inputs per valueType, a provenance badge on every row, requires-restart notice, masked secret, and an atomic save bar carrying expectedVersion.
frames.acceptanceNotes: Every row renders exactly one provenance state derived from EffectiveConfigEntry (set here / inherited from <named scope> / locked by <named scope> / default), never a bare value. The scope chain shows all four tiers with the edited scope marked aria-current. Save is ONE atomic PUT /v1/config carrying expectedVersion from the ETag shown in the scope bar; a partial save is never possible. A secret row shows a mask and a Replace action only, never a value and never a show-toggle. The dirty counter matches the number of changed rows. A requiresRestart key shows the restart notice inline, not only after saving.

frames.label: (b) Provenance, lock & unset-vs-pin
frames.summary: The six distinct EffectiveConfigEntry shapes the editor must render differently — set-here, inherited, locked-by-ancestor, readonly, scope-not-allowed, default — plus the Reset menu that separates `unset` from pinning the parent's current value.
frames.acceptanceNotes: The locked state NAMES the locking scope from lockedBy and shows lockReason verbatim; a generic 'cannot edit' fails this frame. The Reset menu offers TWO operations that must never be collapsed into one control: `unset` (removes this scope's override, keeps tracking the parent forever) and pin-parent-value (`set` with the parent's current value, stops tracking). Both emit the exact ConfigOperation JSON shown. The four reasons a control is disabled — locked, readonly, scope-not-allowed, no Permit grant — are visually distinct and separately selectable, because the user's next action differs in each. scope-not-allowed offers NO enabled input (never a control that only fails on save with SCOPE_NOT_ALLOWED). The default state must not read as empty/unset — the value is real and in force.

frames.label: (c) Editor states — loading, empty, error, hidden-absent
frames.summary: Loading skeleton, empty namespace (a legitimate 200), load error, the proof that system-hidden keys are absent rather than filtered, and a read-only scope rendered fail-closed with no save bar at all.
frames.acceptanceNotes: HIDDEN IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE: hidden keys are omitted by the API and the editor performs NO client-side filtering — QA asserts on the network payload, because a build that fetches hidden keys and hides them with CSS passes any DOM-only assertion while failing the epic's zero-hidden-keys-in-the-browser metric. Empty namespace is distinct from no-search-results and from load error, and offers namespace switching rather than retry. Load error never presents an editable form: with no baseline version there is no safe expectedVersion to send. The read-only scope renders every input disabled AND omits the save bar entirely — never inputs plus a Save button that only 403s.

frames.label: (d) Save failures — conflict, validation, lock, stale value
frames.summary: The four ways a save fails and the different next action each demands: VERSION_CONFLICT re-read-and-merge, per-field VALIDATION_ERROR, LOCKED_BY_ANCESTOR acquired mid-edit, and a stored value that no longer satisfies its updated definition.
frames.acceptanceNotes: VERSION_CONFLICT must drive a per-key re-read-and-merge — showing the server value, the user's value, and a Theirs/Yours choice — and must offer NO blind Retry and NO force-save/overwrite affordance, since the only way to make a blind retry succeed is to drop expectedVersion and destroy the concurrent edit. The conflict view distinguishes a peer edit from an inherited (ancestor) change, because version tracks both. Every failure banner states explicitly that NOTHING was saved — the batch is atomic and 'some changes applied' is the state users cannot reason about. VALIDATION_ERROR renders against the offending input, names what WAS allowed, and disables Save. The stale-value state shows BOTH the default now in force AND the orphaned stored value, so the user's setting does not look silently discarded. Consumers branch on ErrorBody.code, never on message.

frames.label: (e) Key catalog
frames.summary: The platform-admin catalog of every KeyDefinition in a namespace — value type, allowed scopes, system / hidden / secret / readonly / deprecated flags and defaults — and the only surface on which hidden keys are ever visible.
frames.acceptanceNotes: Rows render KeyDefinition fields directly: valueType, allowedScopes, isSystem, isHidden, isSecret, isReadonly, requiresRestart, deprecatedAt/replacedBy, defaultValue. A secret key shows no default value, ever. Hidden rows appear HERE and are absent from every GET /v1/config response the editor makes — the two views must be asserted together, since either alone can pass while the invariant is broken. Reaching this route requires a platform-admin grant; if a non-platform-admin can load this table that is a disclosure bug. This flow is read-only — key definitions are registered declaratively from an app manifest (FF-EPIC-18-S6), not authored in a console form.

frames.label: (f) Definition & diff-against-parent
frames.summary: One KeyDefinition in full, plus the resolution chain that answers 'why is this scope on this value?' — including the no-divergence case and a chain terminated by an ancestor lock.
frames.acceptanceNotes: The chain renders every tier from definition default through platform / portal / org / user, marks the winning step, and states the diff against the parent. It reads definition.precedence rather than assuming most-specific-wins: under least-specific-wins the same chain resolves the other way and the view must follow. The no-divergence case is a designed answer ('no overrides anywhere'), not an empty table. A lock terminates the chain: scopes beneath it render as UNREACHABLE with LOCKED_BY_ANCESTOR named, not merely as 'no override', or an admin will keep trying to set them. Every chain step is a typed Scope (scopeType + scopeId), never a bare id.

frames.label: (g) Catalog states
frames.summary: Loading, and the three empties that look alike and mean different things — no namespaces registered, namespace declares no keys, search matched nothing — plus load error and the fail-closed non-platform-admin refusal.
frames.acceptanceNotes: The three empty states must be separately reachable and separately worded: no-namespaces is a first-run/setup state whose action is documentation; empty-keys names the namespace and points at the owning app; no-results names the active search and filters and offers to clear them, and must be unreachable when the underlying list is genuinely empty. FORBIDDEN is the load-bearing state: because the catalog is the ONLY surface exposing isHidden keys, no definition data may reach the browser at all — QA asserts on the network response, since a spec that only checks 'no rows visible' passes against a build that fetched every hidden key and hid it with CSS.

frames.label: (h) Secret values
frames.summary: The write-only secret field in all six of its states: not set, set (masked, unreadable), replacing, reveal-once, SECRET_UNAVAILABLE, and may-set-but-not-reveal.
frames.acceptanceNotes: value is ALWAYS null for an isSecret key; isSet carries existence. The set state has NO show/reveal toggle on the field, because the browser never received the value — a masked <input> holding real plaintext fails this frame. isSet:false renders the words 'No value set', never an empty mask that claims a credential exists. Replacing starts EMPTY (nothing to pre-fill) and blank-on-save is not the same as Clear. Reveal is a separate, individually authorized, individually audited operation with a required reason, shown exactly ONCE with no re-open — a second look is a new authorization and a new audit entry. SECRET_UNAVAILABLE must NOT be presented as 'not set': telling the user it is unset invites overwriting a working credential that is merely temporarily unreadable. Write and read are separate grants, so may-replace-but-not-reveal is a real state, shown in place rather than as a button that only 403s.

frames.label: (i) Audit history & revert
frames.summary: The append-only change trail with actor, scope, reason and operation; revert-as-a-new-change; a secret key's history redacted on both sides; and the empty / loading / error / forbidden states.
frames.acceptanceNotes: Revert APPENDS, never rewinds: it replays an earlier value as a new set (or a new unset) and the original entry stays in the log — a history that a UI action can shorten is not an audit trail. Reverting to an `unset` entry replays the UNSET (restoring inheritance), not the value it happened to resolve to at the time. A secret key's history is redacted on BOTH sides — an audit log holding secret values is a secret store with worse access control — and 'Revert to this' is ABSENT rather than disabled, since no plaintext exists to revert to; reveals are themselves audited rows. Empty history is 'never changed at this scope' and names where the value does come from; it is not an error and must never read as a gap in the record. Load error and FORBIDDEN are separate states: the error says the record is intact and offers retry, the refusal offers none, so a compliance reviewer never wonders whether the trail was lost. Every actor and scope is a typed reference (scopeType + scopeId), never a bare id.

anticipatedEndpoints: POST /v1/config/secrets/reveal — reveal-once, separately authorized and individually audited (FF-EPIC-18-S1). Must never become a field on the bulk read.
GET /v1/config/history — append-only change trail per (namespace, scope, key), with actor, reason and redacted secret values (FF-EPIC-18-S2).
Revert is NOT a new endpoint — it is a replayed `set`/`unset` through PUT /v1/config, so the revert is itself recorded in history (FF-EPIC-18-S3).
